Hi all — quick notes on KMS and upload practices: 

- Client-side encryption: BrightLeaf can encrypt artifacts with a provided pubkey (attached kms_pubkey.pem). Redwood will accept encrypted objects and will not attempt to decrypt — we store as-is and surface metadata in OneTrust. This is simplest for regulated content.
- Server-side wrap: Redwood KMS wrapping requires an inbound E2E agreement and additional IAM mappings; more work but allows Redwood to run CAIQ validation pipelines.

Recommended: start with client-side pubkey for the first two batches so we can fast-track staging. If BrightLeaf wants Redwood to run automated CAIQ extractions we can pivot to server-side wrap in week two.

S3 upload notes: keep individual object size <15MB for initial staging, include checksum column in manifest. We'll share a signed pre-signed URL workflow for uploads.

Mina Haddad\Cloud Security Engineer\Redwood Inference
